You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC reusable puzzle notes

## Pattern: scatter markers with a sample stamp
Evidence: this instance's demonstrations and solved test; demos show the same rule for several different palettes/template sizes.

- A large uniform-background grid contains a compact exemplar pattern and many isolated marker cells of one color. The exemplar is the stamp; the isolated repeated markers are placement anchors.
- Identify the exemplar's full rectangular bounding box (including its background-colored/blank-looking cells), and identify the anchor within it. In the solved test the exemplar was 3x3 at rows 11–13, columns 6–8; the marker anchor was its center.
- Copy the whole exemplar, preserving its cell colors and background cells, centered/aligned on each isolated marker. Keep the canvas dimensions. Stamps can overlap the exemplar or other cells; apply the copies consistently rather than assuming the exemplar region is protected.
- Check alignment carefully: for the solved 3x3 example, marker at (r,c) got the exemplar at rows r-1..r+1 and columns c-1..c+1. A one-cell offset was the main source of failed attempts. Verify the bottom/right placements independently.
- Include every isolated target marker, including ones near or adjacent to the exemplar. Do not confuse a marker with exemplar cells; use the exemplar's compact patterned region and the repeated scattered color as clues.
- Before submitting, compare a few placements against the exemplar cell-by-cell and ensure dimensions/row lengths remain unchanged. Consider whether the exemplar is overwritten by stamps falling on it; in the solved case, yes, output was formed by stamping all anchors, not preserving the source patch specially.

Solved test's exemplar (rows 11–13, cols 6–8): [[4,5,5],[8,5,8],[8,5,0]]. Each scattered 1 received this centered 3x3 stamp, including the 4 background cells. Test markers: (1,2),(1,9),(6,11),(7,4),(12,2),(13,11),(17,4),(17,8). The accepted output supports copying full pattern including background; the bottom-right stamp at (17,8) was a useful alignment check.
